sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Antimatter**: Composed of **antiparticles** (e.g., positron for electron, antiproton for proton). When matter and antimatter meet, they undergo **annihilation**, converting mass into pure energy (E=mc²).
• **Dark Matter**: Detected only via **gravitational effects** on visible matter (galactic rotation curves, gravitational lensing). It is non-baryonic and does not interact with the electromagnetic force.
• **Baryon Asymmetry**: The unexplained mystery of why the observable universe is dominated by matter despite the Big Bang theoretically producing equal amounts of both.
• **Key Metric**: Dark Matter constitutes ~27% of the universe's energy-mass density, while Dark Energy constitutes ~68%, and ordinary matter only ~5%.

Leading theoretical candidate for dark matter; particles that interact only via gravity and the weak nuclear force.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **PET Scans**: Positron Emission Tomography uses antimatter (positrons) for medical imaging.
• **AMS-02 (Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer)**: A particle physics detector on the International Space Station searching for dark matter and antimatter in cosmic rays.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Detection**: Dark matter is 'dark' because it lacks electromagnetic interaction, making direct detection extremely difficult.
• **Storage**: Antimatter is highly unstable; magnetic traps are required to prevent annihilation with container walls.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'D-A-M' (Dark, Antimatter, Matter).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Dark (Invisible/Gravity), Antimatter (Mirror/Annihilation), Matter (Visible/Baryonic).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Dark Matter' with 'Dark Energy'. Remember: Dark Matter acts as a 'cosmic glue' (attractive gravity), while Dark Energy acts as a 'cosmic expander' (repulsive force).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Baryonic Matter' to distinguish ordinary matter from the 'Dark Sector' in answers regarding the composition of the universe.

keyTakeaways: Antimatter is real and observable in labs; Dark Matter is inferred through gravity.
The universe is dominated by Dark Energy and Dark Matter, not ordinary matter.
CERN and AMS-02 are the primary institutional pillars for current research.
